summary: Reproduced that XGrammarGrammar.rollback replaced and copied the complete accepted-token list, and that rollback(0) cleared the history. Changed rollback to delete the requested tail in place only when the count is nonzero. Added regression coverage for one-token EAGLE-style rollback plus zero, multi-token, and full-history boundaries.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before regression: all three positive rollback cases replaced the accepted_tokens list, and rollback(0) cleared it. Raw output: reports/j-2a43cd4805ed/raw/pytest-before.txt
Passing-after regression and existing speculative tree traversal coverage: 7 tests passed. Raw output: reports/j-2a43cd4805ed/raw/pytest-after.txt

Compared the reported legacy slice operation with the fixed XGrammarGrammar.rollback. Legacy time increased from 0.830 us at 1,000 retained tokens to 89.146 us at 100,000, while fixed rollback remained 0.064-0.066 us. Raw output: reports/j-2a43cd4805ed/raw/rollback-scaling-after.txt

gpu_execution.evidence: The defect and correction are confined to Python list mutation on the scheduler CPU path. No EAGLE-compatible model weights were available or needed for the deterministic implementation-level reproduction, so no GPU or service-level TPOT claim is made.

remaining_limitations: No full EAGLE model serving reproduction or TPOT profile was run because compatible model weights were not provided.
The deterministic regression validates rollback state, allocation-relevant list identity, and EAGLE traversal compatibility; it does not measure end-to-end service latency.
